summary: Doubly-linked list node removal. Unlinks node a2 from its list by patching prev->next (offset +76) and next->prev (offset +72), each guarded on the neighbour pointer being non-zero. If the removed node is the current head (this+0x108), the head advances to node->next. Returns a2, or the new head when the head node itself is removed.

local_names.a2: node to unlink from the doubly-linked list

Read the prev pointer stored at node+72; when non-zero, write the removed node's next pointer (node+76) into prev+76 so the predecessor skips the removed node
Read the next pointer stored at node+76; when non-zero, write the removed node's prev pointer (node+72) into next+72 so the successor skips the removed node
Head update is conditional on the removed node being the current head: this[66] == a2, i.e. this+0x108 == a2
When the head is removed, advance this+0x108 to the removed node's next pointer (node+76) and set result to that new head
Return result: a2 normally, or the new head (node->next) when the removed node was the list head
